title: Instrumentation debt ledger and prioritization
body:
Purpose:
This doc creates a lightweight ledger of known observability gaps (metrics, traces, dashboards), gives a compact definition for each missing/weakly-instrumented signal, and proposes a triage/prioritization rubric + a 6-week sprint plan to chip away at the highest-risk items. The goal is to reduce ‘investigation time-to-insight’ for token-serving incidents and rollout regressions by 30% within Q1.

Scope and assumptions:
- Scope: inference path from API ingress -> routing -> model runtime -> KV cache -> response emission. Includes multi-tenant isolation signals and per-model quality telemetry that are currently under-instrumented.
- Not scope: long-term retention policy (this is surfaced in telemetry-cost project), data residency controls, or downstream BI exports.
- Assumes engineers will instrument metrics/traces using the telemetry SDK (otel + internal wrapper), dashboards built in Grafana, alerts wired to PagerDuty via alert manager.

High-level approach:
1) Maintain a single ledger (this doc) where each row is an observable gap: name, short definition, owner, estimated effort, impact quadrant, instrumentation notes.
2) For each gap define the minimal metric/tracing anchor and an example query to validate.
3) Prioritize by customer impact (SLO breach risk + incident frequency), troubleshooting value (time saved), and implementation cost.
4) Roll out in small increments: instrument -> unit test -> lightweight dashboard -> bake for 2 weeks -> promote to canonical dashboard.

Ledger (sample entries):
- name: per-tenant-prefix-warmth-index
  definition: fraction of requests that hit a warmed KV prefix vs miss, computed per tenant and per route.
  owner: Marcus Liu
  effort: medium (2-3 dev days + one dashboard)
  impact: high (cold-cache incidents cause tail latency spikes)
  instrumentation notes: emit a counter metric kv_prefix_hit{tenant,route} and kv_prefix_miss{tenant,route}; also attach trace attribute kv_prefix_status to runtime span. Example validation query: rate(kv_prefix_miss[5m]) / (rate(kv_prefix_hit[5m]) + rate(kv_prefix_miss[5m]))

- name: model-variant-fanout-latency-buckets
  definition: per-model-variant latency histogram sliced by fanout type (single model, multi-model-fanout, reranker).
  owner: Ana Gómez
  effort: medium-high (3-5 dev days to add histograms and dashboards)
  impact: high (helps identify model combos that increase p95)
  instrumentation notes: use Histo/HD type bucketed latency metric inference_latency_ms_bucket{model_variant,fanout_type,tenant}; tag traces with model_variants list and fanout_type. Provide a panel that shows p50/p95/p99 by variant.

- name: request-routing-fallback-counts
  definition: counts of requests that hit a fallback route (e.g., downgraded model variant / cross-region fallback) with the reason label.
  owner: Samir Patel
  effort: low (1-2 dev days)
  impact: medium (safety and SLA insights)
  instrumentation notes: increment counter routing_fallback_total{reason,from_model,to_model,tenant}. Trace span should include routing_decision=fallthrough and fallback_reason.

- name: token-emission-backpressure-meter
  definition: a rate-meter indicating how frequently the runtime enforces token emission backpressure (e.g., stall/kick timers fired).
  owner: Priya Shah
  effort: medium (2 dev days + test harness)
  impact: medium-high (latent stalls cause client timeouts)
  instrumentation notes: gauge runtime_token_backpressure_active{node,model_variant} and counter token_backpressure_event_total{type,reason}. Correlate with client-side request timeouts in dashboard.

Tracing anchor policy (short):
- Minimal span set: api_ingress -> router (route selection span) -> model_invocation (per target model span) -> kv_cache_lookup -> emission_stream.
- Required span attributes: request_id, tenant_id, route, model_variant(s), sequence_length, kv_prefix_status, routing_decision, batch_size, node_id.
- Sampling: adaptive sampling where traces with p95+ latency or any fallback_reason are always retained; otherwise 0.5% baseline sample. Implement severity-weighted sampling via trace attributes.
- Warmth/causal linking: add a trace tag parent_kv_prefix for traces that resulted from a cached prefix to enable session warmness heatmaps.

Dashboard skeletons (validation-first):
- Investigator mini-dashboard (per-route):
  panels: 1) latency quantiles (p50, p95, p99) by model_variant; 2) recent routing fallback counts (5m, 1h); 3) KV prefix warmth heatmap (tenants x routes); 4) trace-sampled examples (link to trace ids).
  objective: enable fast owner triage for a single degraded route.

- Capacity-pattern dashboard (cluster level):
  panels: aggregate throughput, hottest model_variants by tokens/sec, node-level token emission backpressure, autoscale events, top 10 tenants by burstiness.
  objective: detect capacity hot spots and autoscale misconfiguration.

- Quality-regression sentinel (per-release):
  panels: per-prompt-set correctness rate, per-model hallucination proxy (LM-scored consistency), embeddings drift score.
  objective: early detection of regressions after model rollouts.

Prioritization rubric (one-liner):
- Score = (IncidentFrequencyWeight * Frequency) + (SLORiskWeight * SLOImpact) + (TimeSavedWeight * TroubleshootingValue) - (CostWeight * EstimatedEffort).
- Suggested weights: Frequency 0.3, SLOImpact 0.35, TroubleshootingValue 0.25, Effort 0.1 (normalize to 0-10).
- Use quadrant: Quick Wins (high value, low effort), Strategic (high value, high effort), Nice-to-have (low value, low effort), Backlog (low value, high effort).

Validation and rollout checklist for each ledger item:
1) Unit test that emits metric in local runtime harness.
2) End-to-end smoke that validates presence and cardinality of metric in Prometheus exposition for a synthetic tenant.
3) Add a minimal panel to the Investigator dashboard and a short-runbook note.
4) Let it bake for 2 weeks; collect feedback from oncall.
5) Promote metrics to canonical set and add to instrumentation ownership registry.

6-week sprint plan (high level):
- Week 1: Instrumentation sprint kickoff, implement per-tenant prefix warmth, add instrumentation tests, open PRs.
- Week 2: Add model-variant latency histograms, integrate trace attributes for fanout. Dashboard skeletons in Grafana sandbox.
- Week 3: Implement routing fallback counters and token backpressure meter; add alerts to staging.
- Week 4: Bake, collect oncall feedback, iterate dashboards and refine sampling thresholds.
- Weeks 5-6: Promote stable panels to canonical dashboards, update owner roster, and schedule follow-ups for retention/cost trimming.

Open questions / risks:
- Cardinality risk: tenant-level metrics may explode if not gated. Propose coarse-grained tenant buckets (active, trial, enterprise) and a sampling plan for low-volume tenants.
- Storage/retention: histogram cardinality cost for high-frequency buckets. Consider downsampling rollups after 7 days.
- Trace payload size: adding many attributes inflates spans. We should enforce a small attribute budget and use reference ids to look up richer metadata offline.

Next steps (immediate):
- Marcus: create PR for kv_prefix counters and tests (target end of Week 1).
- Ana: prototype latency histogram in runtime and share initial dashboard XML (end of Week 2).
- Samir: add routing_fallback counters and wire basic alert (end of Week 2).
- Priya: coordinate baseline adaptive sampling change and merge a small config to ensure fallback traces are preserved.
- Ops: carve out a Grafana sandbox space and a short confluence note with dashboard links.

Appendix: short metric definitions (canonical wording):
- inference_latency_ms: histogram of end-to-end request latency (ingress -> emission complete) with labels {tenant,route,model_variant,fanout_type}.
- kv_prefix_hit / kv_prefix_miss: counters incremented at KV lookup completion with labels {tenant,route,prefix_hash_bucket}.
- routing_fallback_total: counter of fallback events with labels {reason,from_model,to_model,tenant}.
- token_backpressure_event_total: counter of backpressure enforcement events with labels {node_id,model_variant,type,reason}.

If this approach looks good we will convert the ledger into a small spreadsheet for sprint tracking and add a column for ‘baked_by_date’ and ‘observability-ticket-id’ (Jira) for handoff into the delivery pipeline.

Notes to reviewers:
- Please focus feedback on the prioritization weights and the cardinality mitigation suggestions.
- If you want ownership changed for any ledger row, leave a short comment or tag the owner.

Changelog:
- 2024-11-05 created initial deck and entry list.
- 2024-11-18 added tracing anchor policy and dashboard skeletons.
- 2024-12-18 updated sprint plan and appended canonical metric wording.
- 2025-01-09 minor edits and collaborator updates.
